title: Confirming Close shows the alert and the status Closed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location has no accounting integration (neither QuickBooks Online nor AccountingHub).
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved labor line of 2.0 hours.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Click the X on the alert.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • An alert reads "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." with an X.
  • The status reads "Closed" with one "Internal" badge next to it.
  • The lines can no longer be edited, as on an invoiced work order.
  • The page moves to the Finance tab, showing the document.

Step 4:

  • The alert closes.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R3: “Confirming completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, cores, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and opens the confirmation of S3-R2.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Closed | "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." | Success alert, fades on its own, with the X every alert has”
  • Key Decisions: “Under the hood, Close creates an invoice marked internal or no charge. The screen says Closed · Internal or Closed · No Charge.”
  • Terminology: “Closed · Internal / Closed · No Charge → how running text, the Close confirmation, the success alert and the Reopen dialog name a closed internal or no-charge work order. On screen the status reads Closed and the one badge next to it reads Internal or No Charge, so the classification shows once. Underneath it is a work order with an internal invoice in the Closed state; the locks of an invoiced work order apply.”
  • Terminology: “Statuses are named as the app names them: Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid and Declined. This feature adds the label Closed, which only the internal invoice carries underneath (Key Decisions); Authorization is a line status, not a work order status.”
